mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility turned positive (from -2.0 to +1.4) over the last two weeks, signaling renewed commuting and adjacent errand-running that lifts retail and recreation footfall over the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -2.0 at t-3w to +1.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining positive for the full window, or RETAIL_REC rises even when WORKPLACES reverses negative.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility crossing above a -1 percent threshold indicates meaningful recovery of public transit use, which precedes an increase in retail and recreation visits within two weeks as commuters resume discretionary stops.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -1.0 percent change from baseline for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -3.4 to -0.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses -1.0, or RETAIL_REC rises without any TRANSIT threshold crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous WORKPLACES increase and RESIDENTIAL decrease jointly indicate a structural shift away from stay-at-home routines, compounding to raise RETAIL_REC more than either series would alone, over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously decreases over the same two-week window
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -2.0 to 1.4 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 5.9 to 4.4 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise despite both WORKPLACES rising and RESIDENTIAL falling concurrently, indicating the joint signal has no added predictive value over single-series models.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has plateaued near a high baseline (39.7 to 43.3) for four weeks, indicating essential-trip demand has saturated; this ceiling effect caps any further behavioral spillover into retail and recreation growth, producing a flat-to-declining RETAIL_REC trend.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM values held between 39.7 and 43.3 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat, showing no coupling between saturation in grocery trips and retail growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility exceeding 5 points signals a seasonal shift away from outdoor recreation (e.g., weather cooling), redirecting discretionary trips toward indoor retail and recreation venues within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -15.9 to -21.1 between t-3w and t-2w, a 5.2 point drop
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop exceeding 5 points, or PARKS stability coincides with RETAIL_REC increases.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has trended downward over the last two weeks (5.9 to 4.4), indicating people are spending less time at home and more time out, which structurally feeds higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 5.9 at t-2w to 4.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its decline, or RETAIL_REC rises while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously increases.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent crossing of WORKPLACES above zero and TRANSIT above -1 percent reflects an early-reopening policy regime where restrictions have eased enough to restore office attendance and transit ridership together, which within two weeks translates into higher retail and recreation activity as combined commuting and errand patterns normalize.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses above 0 percent and TRANSIT crosses above -1 percent in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached 1.4 and TRANSIT reached -0.7 at t-0w, both improved from negative baselines
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT crossing their thresholds simultaneously, or policy regime reverses to tightening restrictions during the window.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility stays below -20 percent for two consecutive weekly means, sustained reduced outdoor park use signals a durable seasonal shift that pushes discretionary activity into retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC within one week of the threshold being met.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -20 percent for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -21.1 at t-2w and -19.7 at t-0w, hovering near -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase the week after PARKS sustains below -20 for two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises while PARKS stays above -20.
